/**
 * Generated by `tsir make:policy`. Answers for the permission `{{permission}}` (ref `{{ref}}`).
 *
 * Register the pair in the `policies` array of `createRegistry(...)`. A service then asks
 * `registry.require({ principal, resource: '{{resource}}', action: '{{action}}', data })`, and this
 * rule decides. It has no imports and takes no container lookups.
 */

/** The part of the policy context this rule reads. Structurally matches the registry's context. */
export interface {{pascal}}Context {
  readonly principal: { readonly subject: string };
  /** What the decision is about: the row or id the service passes in. */
  readonly data: unknown;
  /** The principal's effective permissions, implied roles included. */
  readonly permissions: ReadonlySet<string>;
}

export const {{name}}Ref = '{{ref}}';

export function {{name}}Rule(context: {{pascal}}Context) {
  // Ownership goes here, for example: compare `context.data` with `context.principal.subject`.
  // Until it is written, the answer is the role's: it can never grant more than the role does.
  if (context.permissions.has('{{permission}}')) {
    return { allowed: true, source: 'policy', reason: '{{permission}} is granted by a role' } as const;
  }
  return { allowed: false, source: 'policy', reason: '{{permission}} is not granted' } as const;
}

/** The pair `createRegistry({ policies: [...] })` takes. */
export const {{name}}Policy = [{{name}}Ref, {{name}}Rule] as const;
